mostWorthwhile.text: Making the first star was most worthwhile: the cloud's ignition made a dramatic milestone, while the description clearly distinguished nuclear fusion from an ordinary flame.

leastWorthwhile.text: Checking Light, Fire, Gravity and Pigment produced no available partners, making the search for a route feel somewhat repetitive and unclear.

surprise.text: I expected Gravity to collapse the dense cloud, but Fire was the available partner; Gravity instead helped gather the later Starfield into a Galaxy.

arbitrary.text: First star combining with Air to produce a Starfield felt somewhat arbitrary: the imagery explained repeating the pattern, but not Air's particular role.

continue.text: Yes. The fusion clarification and the closing question about what else a star can give make me curious how the myth will unfold, despite the stretches of unproductive inspection.
